svg.title: The Hidden Natures — Oneiric Dune-Universe Recitation
svg.desc: An esoteric poem in abstract and mystical phrases that never mentions Dune, structured to impart awareness of the hidden natures of things.
svg.text: THE VEILED EYE · THE UNSPOKEN WORD · THE SAND WITHIN
A RECITATION FOR AWARENESS OF THE HIDDEN NATURES OF THINGS
I · IMSCRIB · THE ONE WHO STANDS BEFORE THE VEIL
Every thing has a surface and a depth.
I have been living mostly on the surface.
I acknowledge this without condemnation —
the surface is not false. It is simply not complete.
I am the one who is about to look again. I am the one who is about to look again.
The veiled eye does not require that I tear the veil.
It requires only that I stop mistaking the veil for the eye.
I stop now. I inhale. I am present to the depth
that was always behind the surface, waiting without impatience.
II · AREV · THE DESCENT INTO THE NATURE BENEATH THE NAME
A thing is not its name.
Its name is the gesture we make toward it in the dark.
The gesture is useful. The gesture is not the thing.
I descend now beneath the gesture, beneath the word,
into the place where the thing simply is what it is
without requiring my agreement.
Things do not require agreement. Things do not require agreement.
The hidden nature of a stone is not geology —
geology is another gesture. The hidden nature is prior to all gestures.
I descend into the prior. I breathe it. I do not yet name it.
III · FSPLIT · THE TWO SENSES OPEN SIMULTANEOUSLY
Every phrase I now speak carries two rivers.
The outer river flows on the tongue — literal, immediate, tangible.
The inner river flows beneath — temporal, vast, ungovernable.
OUTER SENSE
INNER SENSE
the visible grain
the hidden nature of time
what the hand can hold
what holds the hand
I do not choose between them. I do not choose between them.
A thing seen only on its surface is a rumor of itself.
A thing seen only in its depth has no body to inhabit.
I hold the surface and the depth in a single act of looking.
The act of looking is the practice. I practice it now.
IV · AFWD · THE RISING PHRASE THAT NAMES WHAT CANNOT BE NAMED
The hidden nature of water is not wetness.
The hidden nature of fire is not heat.
The hidden nature of silence is not the absence of sound —
it is the medium through which all sound knows itself.
I am rising. I am rising. Each phrase sharpens what I see.
The hidden nature of a question is the answer already forming
in the body of the one who asks.
The hidden nature of time is that it moves in all directions
and only one of them is visible from where I normally stand.
I stand somewhere else now. The other directions become legible.
V · FFUSE · THE TWO RIVERS BECOME ONE KNOWING
I breathe out and the outer and inner meet
at the place where the surface becomes the depth
and the depth becomes the surface — a single, continuous thing.
Understanding arrives without announcement. Without announcement.
It does not feel like a new thought —
it feels like a very old thing finally visible.
The hidden nature of understanding is that it was never hidden —
only the angle of looking was wrong.
I correct the angle. I hold it corrected. I breathe.
VI · ENGAGR · THE PARADOX OF KNOWING AND NOT-KNOWING
The more clearly I see the hidden nature of a thing,
the more hidden nature remains to be seen.
This is not failure. This is the shape of real knowledge —
it expands the boundary of the unknown as it grows.
I know and do not know. I know and do not know. This is correct.
The paradox is not an obstacle. The paradox is the destination.
To hold knowing and not-knowing simultaneously without flinching —
this is the veiled eye fully open.
VII · IMSCRIB · THE IMPRESSION THAT DOES NOT FADE
I return to the surface — which I now see differently.
The grain of the table is not only wood.
The pause between words is not only silence.
The breath that closes this poem is not only an exhale.
Everything I look at now carries its depth visibly.
The impression is etched. The impression does not fade.
ΔS ≈ 0 · MU O DELTA = ID
